author: vanaukenk
body:
Hi,

I wanted to use the ontology editors functionality to generate spreadsheets for review of annotations to succinate dehydrogenase (quinone) activity (GO:0008177) for standardizing the gp2term relation used, i.e. 'enables' or 'contributes to'.

Would it be possible to update the annotation downloads functionality to include the gp2term relation?

This information might also be helpful to curators in other annotation reviews, e.g. BP annotations, to see the spectrum of gp2term relations used so we can start to standardize better.
title: Can we add gp2term relations to annotation review downloads?

author: pgaudet
body: @kltm Can this be added ? Otherwise we can do the query in AmiGO, as a temporary solution.

author: kltm
body: @pgaudet @vanaukenk Just to be clear, could I get a little sampler of what you'd like the output to look like here?

author: pgaudet
body:
CURRENT

BHF-UCL	UniProtKB:Q9NQR4	NIT2	PMID:22674578	**involved_in**	GO:0006528	asparagine metabolic process	IDA		UniProtKB:Q9NQR4	PANTHER:PTHR23088	20140516		NCBITaxon:9606

author: vanaukenk
body:
Thanks @kltm @pgaudet 

Yes, rather than just returning a qualifier when it exists, e.g. 'contributes to' or 'colocalizes with', the downloads would return every gp2term relation for each standard annotation.

Here's a specific example with an existing BP annotation:

Before:

MGI:MGI:1914523	NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase subunit A10		GO:0006120		MGI	NCBITaxon:10090	IDA		PANTHER:PTHR10513	protein	MGI:MGI:1914523	PMID:24652937	20150421

After:

MGI:MGI:1914523	NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase subunit A10   **acts_upstream_of_or_within**		GO:0006120		MGI	NCBITaxon:10090	IDA		PANTHER:PTHR10513	protein	MGI:MGI:1914523	PMID:24652937	20150421

author: kltm
body: @pgaudet @vanaukenk Okay, I think I understand what you want here, but I don't think we really have this information populated in AmiGO/GOlr or the GO API yet. We can start heading in that direction, but we're probably cruising out of the scope of "one more thing real fast".

author: vanaukenk
pgaudet
body: We can leave it open. I added 'technical issue' for lack of a better label, but it seems we need many changes upstream to be able to do this.
